en: The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, the Treasury of Universal Knowledge;
translated anew by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Dharmacandra in the Kingdom of Magadha.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the great city of Rājagṛha, together with...

There was a great assembly of bhikṣus numbering one hundred thousand, together with seventy-seven thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, headed by such eminent leaders as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and Maitreya Bodhisattva.
All had attained samādhi and dhāraṇī, and dwelt in inconceivable liberation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, who was seated there among them, rose from his seat and approached the World-Honored One.
Facing the Buddha with palms joined, bowing with deep reverence, and gazing up at the Honored One’s countenance, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I wish, within this assembly, to expound the Heart of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Universal Wisdom Treasury of all Bodhisattvas.”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me leave to speak, so that I may proclaim the essential secret Dharma for the sake of all bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara with his wondrous Brahma-voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O you who possess great compassion, listen to what you have said; it shall serve as a great illumination for all sentient beings.

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having received the Buddha’s permission and being protected by the Buddha’s mindfulness, entered the meditative absorption of the Samādhi of Wisdom-Light.

Having entered this meditative absorption, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* through the power of samādhi, he perceives that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty.
Having realized that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty, he calmly arises from that samādhi.
He then addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: "Good son!
Bodhisattvas possess the heart of the Perfection of Wisdom, named the Treasury of Universal Knowledge."
"Listen now attentively and reflect upon it well;
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Having spoken these words, he continued:
The Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"O Great Purifier! I pray that you will explain this for us."
"Now is precisely the right time.
At this, he addressed Śāriputra:
"All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in this manner."
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.
Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form.
Form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also like this.
The nature of consciousness is emptiness, and the nature of emptiness is consciousness.
Consciousness is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from consciousness.
Consciousness is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself consciousness.
Śāriputra, this mark of the emptiness of all phenomena is neither born nor extinguished; it is neither defiled nor pure; it neither increases nor decreases.

Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or phenomena; and no眼界 (eye-element) up to and including no意識界 (consciousness-element).
There is no ignorance, nor is there the exhaustion of ignorance; and so on, up to: there is no old age and death, nor is there the exhaustion of old age and death.
There is no suffering, no accumulation, no cessation, and no path; there is no wisdom, nor is there anything to be attained.
Because there is nothing to be apprehended, the Bodhisattva, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, has no mental hindrance.
Because there is no hindrance, there is no fear; being far removed from perverted dreams and delusions, one attains ultimate Nirvana.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Therefore, know that the Prajñāpāramitā is the great divine mantra, the great illuminating mantra, the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra; it is able to eliminate all suffering, being true and not false.
"Therefore, I proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā mantra.
He then spoke the mantra:

"Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the assembly of bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, as well as all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom, the Treasury of Universal Knowledge.
